requirements:
Application Architecture Requirements (Production Blueprint)

Purpose
- Define a complete, implementable production application architecture equivalent to the reference diagram.
- The architecture must support secure internet ingress, API mediation, web application hosting, microservice execution, data persistence, secrets management, observability, and DR.

Scope
- Environment: Production.
- Primary region: North Europe.
- Secondary/DR region: West Europe.
- Platform: Azure.
- Workload type: Web application + API-managed function microservices.

1) Mandatory Architecture Layers

1.1 Edge / CDN Layer
- Must include Azure Front Door Premium with WAF enabled.
- Must include global edge routing with primary and secondary origin strategy.
- Must include private-link capable origin connectivity where supported.
- Must include DNS strategy for private name resolution of internal dependencies.

1.2 DMZ / Ingress Layer
- Must include Application Gateway (WAF v2) in DMZ VNet.
- Public ingress must terminate at Front Door and then flow to Application Gateway only.
- Public IP on Application Gateway must be restricted to approved upstream origin usage.

1.3 Internal Application Layer
- Must include one App Service (Linux) web application.
- Must include Azure API Management (Premium tier) as API front door for backend APIs.
- Must include function app fleet for domain microservices.
- APIM must route to backend functions over private network paths.

1.4 Data Layer
- Must include PostgreSQL Flexible Server primary in North Europe.
- Must include PostgreSQL DR/geo-restore target in West Europe.
- Database access must be private; no direct public data access.

1.5 Security / Secrets Layer
- Must include Azure Key Vault with private endpoint.
- Access model must be RBAC-based.
- Secret/certificate/key rotation process must be enforced.

1.6 Observability / SOC Layer
- Must include Application Insights for app/APIM/functions telemetry.
- Must include central Log Analytics workspace for retention and archive strategy.
- Must include diagnostics forwarding suitable for SOC/SIEM integration.

1.7 Management Layer
- Must include dedicated management VNet and bastion-style admin path.
- Admin access must be management-only (no use of business ingress path).
- Must support JIT/PIM style administrative controls.

2) Required Resource Inventory (Names/Tiers)

2.1 Networking and Edge
- vnet-aai-prod-dmz-neu-01 (DMZ VNet)
- vnet-aai-prod-ndmz-neu-02 (Internal App VNet)
- vnet-aai-prod-gw-neu-03 (Gateway/Shared Services VNet)
- vnet-aai-prod-mngt-neu-04 (Management VNet)
- fd-aai-prod-neu-01 (Azure Front Door Premium)
- waf-aai-prod-neu-01 (WAF policy)
- ag-aai-prod-agw-neu-01 (Application Gateway WAF v2)
- pip-aai-prod-agw-neu-01 (Application Gateway public IP, restricted usage)

2.2 Runtime and API
- app-aai-prod-wapp-neu-01 (App Service Linux)
- asp-aai-prod-wapp-neu-01 (App Service Plan, Premium v3 class)
- apim-aai-prod-neu-02 (API Management Premium v2, zone-redundant)

2.3 Function Apps (17 logical workloads)
- func-aai-perf-token-neu-01 (Auth token)
- func-aai-perf-shop-offer-neu-02 (Shop/Flights)
- func-aai-perf-services-neu-03 (Services)
- func-aai-perf-seat-services-neu-04 (Seat services)
- func-aai-perf-seat-map-neu-05 (Seat map)
- func-aai-perf-searchpanel-neu-06 (Search panel)
- func-aai-perf-retrieve-order-neu-07 (Retrieve order)
- func-aai-perf-retrieve-cart-neu-08 (Retrieve cart)
- func-aai-perf-rbac-pending-neu-09 (RBAC pending/domain-specific)
- func-aai-perf-payment-neu-10 (Payment)
- func-aai-perf-create-cart-neu-11 (Create cart)
- func-aai-perf-checkoutupdate-neu-12 (Checkout update)
- func-aai-perf-checkoutpassengers-neu-13 (Checkout passengers)
- func-aai-perf-checkoutinitiate-neu-14 (Checkout initiate)
- func-aai-perf-checkoutconfirm-neu-15 (Checkout confirm)
- func-aai-perf-baggage-policies-neu-16 (Baggage policies)
- func-aai-perf-appconfigp-neu-17 (App config)

2.4 Data/Security/Telemetry
- psql-aai-prod-data-neu-01 (Primary PostgreSQL Flexible Server)
- psql-aai-prod-dr-weu-01 (DR PostgreSQL target)
- kv-aai-prod-neu-01 (Key Vault)
- law-aai-prod-security-neu-01 (Log Analytics workspace)

3) API and Domain Coverage Requirements
- APIM must expose and route at least the following API domains:
  - appconfig
  - cart-retrieve
  - checkout-confirm
  - checkout-passengers
  - checkout-update
  - create-cart
  - order-retrieve
  - payment
  - searchpanel
  - seatmap
  - seat-services
  - service
  - shop-offer
  - func-token
- APIM and backends must support private VNet integration and centralized diagnostics.

4) Network Segmentation Requirements

4.1 VNet and Subnet Policy
- Each VNet must be dedicated to a trust domain (DMZ, app internal, gateway/shared, management).
- Subnets must be separated by role and traffic profile.
- At minimum, represent and enforce NSG boundaries for:
  - nsg-aai-prod-dmz-neu-01
  - NSG ndmz-app
  - NSG ndmz-ilb
  - NSG ndmz-data
  - NSG mgmt
  - NSG bastion
  - NSG gateway
- Any public endpoint must be explicitly justified; default is private access.

4.2 Private Endpoints and DNS
- Private endpoints must be used for App/API/data/security critical paths where applicable.
- Private DNS zones must support resolution for:
  - PostgreSQL
  - Key Vault
  - App Service
  - APIM

5) Traffic and Access Control Requirements

5.1 North-South Flow
- Internet -> Front Door -> Application Gateway -> Web App/APIM.
- No direct internet access to function apps, data stores, or Key Vault.

5.2 East-West Flow
- APIM -> Function Apps over private paths.
- Web App/Functions -> PostgreSQL over private paths.
- Function Apps -> Key Vault over private paths.

5.3 Administrative Flow
- Management VNet/Bastion path must be separate from business traffic path.
- Administrative actions must require role-based elevation and auditable controls.

6) Security Controls Requirements
- WAF must be deployed at edge and/or ingress per policy.
- RBAC must be used for service authorization and operator access.
- Managed identities must be used for service-to-service secret retrieval.
- Key Vault must be authoritative source for secrets/certs/keys.
- Rotation policy must exist and be evidenced in operations documentation.

7) High Availability, Deployment, and DR Requirements
- APIM in Premium tier must be zone-redundant.
- Database primary must be HA-capable; DR target must be defined in secondary region.
- Front Door must support failover origin behavior across regions.
- App tier must support deployment slot strategy (staging/pre-prod swap).
- Blue/green deployment approach must be supported for critical runtimes.
- DR runbooks, health probes, and failover criteria must be documented.

8) Observability and SOC Requirements
- Application Insights must collect telemetry from:
  - Web App
  - APIM
  - Critical Function Apps
- Log Analytics workspace must centralize logs and enforce retention/archive policy.
- Alerting and dashboard coverage must include availability, latency, failures, and security signals.
- Diagnostic pipelines must support SOC consumption.

9) Naming and Standards Requirements
- Resource names must encode workload, environment, region, and sequence.
- Production naming should follow the existing pattern shown in section 2.
- Diagram legend must distinguish traffic classes:
  - HTTPS traffic
  - API routing
  - Function calls
  - DB connections
  - Telemetry
  - Secret access
  - Admin/management traffic
  - DR/failover path

10) Diagram Composition Requirements
- The diagram must explicitly show:
  - Layer containers and trust boundaries.
  - All VNets and key NSG boundaries.
  - All critical resources listed in section 2.
  - Directional arrows for all mandatory flows.
  - Primary vs DR region elements and failover context.
  - Security and observability components connected to workloads.
- The diagram must include a legend and line semantics.

11) Non-Functional Requirements
- Security: zero-trust posture, least privilege, private-by-default internal connectivity.
- Reliability: zone resilience for critical control plane and app/API tiers.
- Recoverability: region-level DR posture for data and edge failover.
- Operability: centralized logging/metrics/tracing and actionable alerting.
- Maintainability: modular API domains and clear service ownership per function app.

12) Acceptance Criteria (Architecture Complete)
- All mandatory layers are present and connected per required flow.
- No prohibited direct paths exist (for example internet -> data/key vault/function).
- Private endpoints and DNS strategy are represented for internal dependencies.
- DR components and failover intent are represented and consistent.
- Management path is isolated and auditable.
- A reviewer can recreate the reference architecture from this document without missing critical components or flows.


--- CLARIFIED REQUIREMENTS ---
[SCALE] What are the expected peak and average load characteristics for the web application and API tiers (e.g., concurrent users, requests per second)?: 250 concurrent users
[SECURITY] Are there specific compliance standards or regulatory requirements (e.g., GDPR, ISO 27001) that the architecture must adhere to?: GDPR
[INTEGRATION] Do any external systems or third-party integrations need to be supported (e.g., payment gateways, external APIs)?: Payment gateway and Amadeus Nevio API
[PERFORMANCE] Are there specific latency or throughput performance targets for API and microservice calls?: latency < 1000 ms and throughput 20 rps
[BUSINESS] Are there any constraints or priorities regarding operational budget or cost optimization for the architecture?: strict budget
[DISASTER RECOVERY] What is the maximum acceptable recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) for disaster recovery scenarios?: RTO<5 mins RPO<15 mins
